summary: On Linux require authenticated replication-worker process provenance on worker-only internal routes before reading request bodies.

replay.detail: Retired claim IDs remain valid reconciliation data through the authenticated worker; no claim format change.

compatibility.detail: On Linux unrelated unbound Unix callers and browser callers receive worker-authentication-required on worker-only routes. macOS retains existing admission and emits unverified-platform; its unbound local caller authority gap remains open because live-PID socket credentials do not establish the original connector generation. Operator fleet routes are unchanged. No transferable token is added.

downtime.detail: Roll the daemon and supervised worker together. Daemon-first is supported when the worker restarts in the same step; requests may retry during the restart. A new worker with the old daemon retains its previous behavior. An old supervised worker remains identifiable by its supervisor and kernel generation, but coordinated restart is required operationally.

manual.detail: Without services, start replication-worker first and start the daemon with up --replication-worker-pid PID. Restart the foreground daemon with the new PID whenever the worker is restarted. Service-managed daemons refuse this startup option.

recovery.detail: Restore the supervised worker or restart the foreground daemon with its current worker PID. Same-UID service-manager takeover and ptrace of the trusted worker remain outside this boundary.
